segments.line: On the TV, lying sideways on the floor, a man in a suit is talking.
Every news anchor on Earth is lying down. He's
a scientist. 'We can measure it to the millisecond, ' he says. 'It doubles at exactly the top of the hour. Not near it. Exactly. '
Then he says the thing that makes your mom go quiet.
'Something is doing this on purpose. Nature doesn't keep a schedule. '
The planes come first. Every pilot in the sky is trying to land before nine.
An airliner is only built to handle about two and a half g. They have a few minutes.
Then the satellites. Every one of them is going around the Earth at a speed set for normal gravity. Now they're too slow. The lowest ones start to fall.
Down here, hospitals move every patient onto the floor. Firefighters can't climb their own ladders.
And somewhere over the ocean, a pilot radios the tower. 'We're coming down early. We don't have a choice. '
Then the man in the suit says the one useful thing anyone says all day.
'If you can, get into water. Water pushes up on you. And the stronger gravity gets, the harder it pushes back. '
That's real. A floating body is held up by the water around it. Double the gravity, and the push of the water doubles too.
Your mom looks at you. You look at her. You both think the same thing.
Mr. Patel next door has a swimming pool.
It's eight forty- one. Nineteen minutes.
